name: Next drive: friction relay A/B (identification tests optional)

windows.amount: pulses 54 s, ladder 60 s, sweep about 80 s (credited seconds), if they happen
windows.reason: Optional: the owner's decision, 'alteration alone is fine'. At the tests' signal sizes the steering wheel's response is below the angle sensor's resolution, the torque-sensor path is already measured, and the car model is frozen below the limit, so these tests no longer justify a required stretch of driving. They run and are credited when the road allows, everywhere outside the alternation's range from the start and inside it once the alternation is complete.
windows.minimum: None required. Pulses 54 s, ladder 60 s and sweep about 80 s are what would complete this window if it happens.

windows.amount: sweep 67 s, pulses 80 s, ladder 100 s, if they happen
sweep 57 s, pulses 72 s, ladder 85 s, if they happen
sweep 41 s, pulses 74 s, ladder 75 s, if they happen

alternation.reason: The question is whether removing the friction relay reduces steering oscillation (direction reversals per second) at the A/B speeds (36-63 mph since 2026-11-22; the variation below was measured at 36-55 mph). Pass-to-pass variation is about 0.12 per second per pass of about 86 s; the one earlier comparison showed a drop of about 0.23 per second, about 1.9 times that variation.
alternation.minimum: About 4-5 passes per side (about 6-7 minutes per side) give 80 percent power for an effect of that size. It cannot show an effect as small as closed-loop replay predicted (about 0.05 per second): that would need well over an hour per side and is out of reach of any single drive.
alternation.buffer: 10 minutes per side is that minimum plus about half again, so a second drive is unlikely to be needed.

priority: the alternation has 35-64 mph (36-63 shown) until it is complete: nothing optional takes time from it; 57-63 mph was a gap where nothing counted (2026-11-22 drive)
the optional tests run everywhere else from the start, and everywhere once it is complete
